facts.material: 100 percent cotton cheesecloth (woven, not pile or terry), two layers, tannin pre-mordant treated
facts.form: 6 x 6 inch squares, two layers sewn with overlock stitch; unfinished (charcoal dye and decorative zigzag border added after importation)
facts.end_use: personal facial cleansing and exfoliation, sold at retail in packs of two

gri_path: GRI 2(a): the imported cut, layered and overlocked squares already have the size, shape and construction of the finished facial cloth; post-importation dyeing and decorative stitching do not change its identity, so it is classified as the finished article
GRI 1: heading 6302 toilet linen covers face cloths/washcloths; chapter 63 note 1 (made up articles) satisfied by cutting to shape and sewing; section XI note 7 made up
GRI 6: 6302.91 other toilet linen of cotton (not terry toweling, 6302.60, since cheesecloth is not terry); not of pile or tufted construction
GRI 6: statistical suffix under Other: Towels: Other: Other (369), 6302.91.00.50

rejected_alternatives.reason: cheesecloth is a plain open weave, not terry toweling
that suffix is for cotton towels of pile or tufted construction
residual made-up articles; 6302 toilet linen is more specific for reusable face cloths
article is made up (cut to shape and sewn), so not piece-goods fabric of chapter 52

classification.rationale: The imported squares are made up articles with the essential character of the finished facial cloth, so GRI 2(a) classifies them as the finished good. Facial cloths and exfoliating face mitts are toilet linen of heading 6302 (NY N327013 placed an exfoliating facial mitt in 6302.93). Because the fabric is cotton woven cheesecloth, not terry and not pile, it falls in 6302.91.00, and as a towel-type face cloth it takes the Towels: Other: Other (369) suffix .50.
